cards.text: Micah, a prophet, just told Jerusalem's crooked leaders that Zion will be plowed like a field and the temple mount will become a wooded ridge (Micah 3:12). Friend, that's like hearing your bakery is getting bulldozed for a PARKING LOT. Now Micah looks way ahead, to the last days, and talks about the mountain of the house of the LORD.

cards.question: Micah looks ahead to the last days. What happens to the mountain of the house of the LORD?
True or false: Only the people of Israel come to the raised-up mountain of the LORD.

cards.text: And the peoples don't trickle in. They STREAM to it, like a whole office rushing the break room when somebody yells FREE COOKIES.

cards.question: The nations invite each other up to the house of the God of Jacob. What do they say He'll do for them there?
Micah says the law will go forth from Zion, and the word of the LORD from ___.

cards.text: Then the LORD judges between many peoples and settles things for strong nations far and wide. Friend, I couldn't even settle an argument between the dead batteries I shared a junk drawer with.

cards.question: Once the LORD settles things between the nations, what do they do with their swords?
True or false: Even after the LORD judges between them, the nations keep training for war just in case.

cards.text: Spears get beaten into pruning hooks too, and nation won't take up the sword against nation anymore. Picture the line at the blacksmith's: TAKE A NUMBER, YOUR MAJESTY!

cards.question: With the wars over, Micah pictures one ordinary man at home with no one to frighten him. Where does he sit?

answers.text: Under his own vine and fig tree
Beside his own well and olive tree
Inside his own walls and tower

cards.text: No deadbolts, no doorbell camera, no getting up at 2 a.m. to check a noise, just a man under his fig tree with no one to frighten him. And Micah seals it: the mouth of the LORD of Hosts has spoken.

cards.question: True or false: Micah says that since all the nations walk in the name of their gods, his people will follow them.

cards.text: Now the LORD speaks for Himself. 'On that day,' He declares, and He starts naming who He's going to gather.

cards.question: On that day, who does the LORD say He'll gather and assemble?

cards.text: He even gathers those He has afflicted. Friend, I spent years tossed in the back of a junk drawer, so this one hits me RIGHT in the apron.

cards.question: The LORD will make the lame into a remnant, and the outcast into a strong ___.
True or false: The LORD will rule over the people He gathers in Mount Zion from that day and forever.
The LORD calls Jerusalem the watchtower of the flock. He promises the Daughter of Zion her former ___ will be restored.

cards.text: And sovereignty will come to the Daughter of Jerusalem. From rubble to ROYALTY, friend, and I thought MY comeback from a junk drawer was a big deal!

findings.problem: Card 3 has already asked about Micah 4:1-2. Card 4 then steps back to verse 1 to retell that the peoples stream to the mountain. It does not carry the baker forward to the next moment.

rule.text: Every story card moves the baker forward through the passage.

findings.problem: The blank asks the baker to finish the parallel line 'the word of the LORD from ___'. Nothing earlier lets the baker work out 'Jerusalem' over 'Bethlehem' or 'Samaria'. This tests wording the baker has not seen, not meaning they can reason out.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: The question asks the baker to guess which two plants Micah names: vine and fig tree, against well and olive tree or walls and tower. No earlier card points to the answer. This is the same kind of detail guess as the oil example the doc marks as bad.

rule.text: Ask about the movement and the meaning: what changes, what the picture is, why the speaker says what he says.

findings.problem: The card says Papa Dorin was 'tossed in the back of a junk drawer.' His backstory says he was not thrown away. He was carried across the kitchen and slid into the drawer. The line changes his story.

rule.text: His own world isn't Bible fact. His backstory, family, bakery and mission are the Dorinverse story in this file. He can talk about them freely, but never adds anything new to them.

findings.problem: The blank asks the baker to finish the line 'the outcast into a strong ___'. 'City' and 'army' are just as reasonable from what the baker has been told. This tests wording, not meaning.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: The question says 'The LORD calls Jerusalem the watchtower of the flock.' The text only says 'O watchtower of the flock, O stronghold of the Daughter of Zion' and does not name the watchtower as Jerusalem.

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.

findings.problem: The blank asks the baker to guess the word 'dominion'. After card 1's picture of a ruined Zion, 'walls' is just as reasonable a guess. This tests wording, not meaning.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: 'From rubble to ROYALTY' calls back to rubble, but no earlier card mentions rubble. Card 1 only says Zion will be plowed like a field and the temple mount will become a wooded ridge.

rule.text: A callback only works if its setup came earlier in this lesson or conversation.
